result_summary: No pre-determined RBF bandwidth lifts the shipped linear pre-pass. All five grid bandwidths passed the kill-gate (none is a monotone copy: lowest cost Spearman over the 11 gate pools 0.9816 for m = 0.25 down to -0.0664 for m = 64) and were scored on the three panels. With the top-1 coordinate dropped: conditioned contrast 2.489, 2.494, 2.336, 1.913, 0.269 for m = 0.25, 1, 4, 16, 64 against shipped 2.413 and the required 2.655 (largest gain 3.4% against 10%), selection-axis violations 0, 0, 0, 4, 22 of 28; ibm symmetric margin +19.04, +16.25, +6.11, +0.00, -9.54 against shipped +19.41; Wergeland margin +53.90, +50.26, +33.00, +6.78, -1.60 against shipped +54.74. m = 0.25 meets the two margin clauses and not the contrast clause; every other bandwidth meets none. Second readings give the same outcome: with nothing dropped no bandwidth meets every clause (m = 0.25: contrast 2.694 = 1.116x with 2/28 violations), and the registered margins change no clause. Mechanism: at m = 0.25 the kernel is close to affine in the cosine (R2 0.9927) and its dropped coordinate agrees with the linear one at 0.9998, so its readings stay within 0.83 points and 3.1% of the shipped ones; narrower kernels put most statement pairs at nearly the same distance (R2 0.3723, 0.0464, 0.0356 for m = 4, 16, 64) and the margins fall. On the conditioned triples the cosines do not form one narrow band (mean 0.6092; 28 of 70 source statements have under 5 words) and the top component lies mostly on those short statements (loading 0.696 linear, 0.899 at m = 64). Reading without a bar, with the E14-H76 word rules: with the 22 one-word source statements removed no arm that holds the margins meets the contrast clause (0.923 to 0.975x shipped); with the 28 statements under 5 words removed the nothing-dropped arms meet it at 0/28 violations - linear kernel 1.206x, m = 0.25 1.193x, m = 1 1.109x - so that effect is centering alone (the E14-H76 finding) and the RBF kernel does not add to it. On those shorter sources m = 16 and m = 64 read contrast ratios of 4.460x to 2248.192x with DR at 0.8% to 13.2% of the shipped DR: a collapse of the scale, with ibm symmetric margins of +0.00 and -9.54.
caveats: (1) Verdict label: the record ties Confirmed to 'kernel PCA lifts the pre-pass' and Refuted to 'at least one bandwidth passes the gate and none meets every clause'. Refuted is the outcome on the bar that the hypothesis predicted; direction_matched is false because one predicted effect did not match (m = 0.25 and m = 1 are not monotone copies: 0.9940 on the ibm symmetric pool against 0.995, 0.9816 to 0.9854 on the triples) and the stability part holds only under the executor's aggregation. (2) Verdict rule changed after the first execution: the notebook first applied its own triangle-slack reading (1e-09 through the shipped cost_matrix in float64, a tolerance the record does not register) to every geometry and printed Blocked, because the RBF arms read +5.3e-09 to +3.7e-08. The reading and its tolerance are unchanged and still reported as exceeded; a diagnostic located the excess on statement pairs closer than 1e-06 (repeated source statements that the float32 kernel map returns at a non-zero distance), and Blocked is now decided by the guardrails the record and the primer register, which all hold. If the standing 'metric property untouched' guardrail is meant to cover prototype geometries under that exact reading, this result reads Blocked instead of Refuted; no acceptance clause or kill-gate reading depends on it. (3) Order: the harness check runs before the kill-gate, as the task notes say, because the gate reads its costs from the map under check; the primer lists the kill-gate first. Both cells execute before the panel cells. (4) Conditioned panel: the E14-H76 notebook did not exist when this task started and existed at 11:49, before the first execution; its panel code is used (E04 helpers verbatim and text-checked, a = document, b = anchor, anchor-against-itself triple for the E04 count over 28 orderings; the count without the anchor, over 24, is the same on every scored arm). The raw and shipped DR (0.034535, 0.219067) equal the E14-H76 key numbers to every digit; the linear nothing-dropped arm reads DR 0.119861 = 0.5471x shipped with 1/28 violations, the reading of arm a in E14-H76 to 6 decimals (E14-H76 computes arm a without an eigen-decomposition). (5) Executor's rules, stated in the configuration cell, which executes before the measurement cells: costs in float64 on exact-unit copies over distinct pairs; the bar read on the top-1-dropped arm; thresholds from the shipped row of this run (2.6547, +18.41, +53.74); reference rows within 0.005 points (observed differences 0.0017, 0.0044, 0.0043); bootstrap stability as the feature-space cosine of the top component over 50 resamples with replacement, read on the mean over the 11 gate pools; 'every pool' as the 11 gate pools plus the Wergeland pool. Every second reading is printed beside the rule's reading. (6) The stability part holds by 0.007 and 0.012 and the ibm symmetric pool alone carries it; without replacement (80% subsamples) that pool reads 0.632 and 0.798 for m = 16 and m = 64. (7) The hypothesis quotes a pooled mean cosine of 0.736 for the triples; the per-triple pools on the shipped path read 0.6092. The two shorter sources of the reading without a bar are row removals from the same embeddings, not a re-segmentation. (8) One conditioned fixture: one source, one anchor, 10 documents, 4 adversarial; the contrast is a ratio of two tier means and grows when the scale of D_sel collapses. (9) Additions outside the record, all without a bar: the linear-kernel nothing-dropped reference arm, the panel without the short source statements, subsample stability, affine-fit R2, top-coordinate agreement, loading on short source statements, unclipped margins (largest effect 0.79 pts, no margin clause changes), the triangle diagnostic.
